name.quote: The examining committee, heretofore created pursuant to RCW 43.24.060, is reorganized and reconstituted as the optometry board.

type.quote: The board has the following powers and duties: (1) To develop and administer, or approve, or both, a licensure examination.

umbrella_agency.quote: obtaining a license from the secretary of health

degree_required.quote: Have a diploma or other certificate of completion from an accredited college of optometry or school of optometry, maintaining a standard which is deemed sufficient and satisfactory by the optometry board, conferring its degree of doctor of optometry or its equivalent

accrediting_body.quote: from an accredited college of optometry or school of optometry, maintaining a standard which is deemed sufficient and satisfactory by the optometry board

exams.quote: To develop and administer, or approve, or both, a licensure examination. The board may approve an examination prepared or administered by a private testing agency or association of licensing authorities.

available.quote: An applicant holding a credential in another state may be credentialed to practice in this state without examination if the board determines that the other state's credentialing standards are substantially equivalent to the standards in this state.

requirements.value: Credentialing by endorsement available if the other state's credentialing standards are substantially equivalent to Washington's standards.
requirements.quote: An applicant holding a credential in another state may be credentialed to practice in this state without examination if the board determines that the other state's credentialing standards are substantially equivalent to the standards in this state.

scope_protection.quote: To practice optometry in this state either for him or herself or any other individual, corporation, partnership, group, public or private entity, or any member of the licensed healing arts without having at the time of so doing a valid license issued by the secretary of health

disciplinary_grounds.description: Any form of fraud or deceit used in securing a license.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any form of fraud or deceit used in securing a license

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any unprofessional conduct, of a nature likely to deceive or defraud the public

disciplinary_grounds.quote: The employing either directly or indirectly of any person or persons commonly known as "cappers" or "steerers" to obtain business

disciplinary_grounds.description: Employing any person to solicit from house to house, or personally soliciting from house to house.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: To employ any person to solicit from house to house, or to personally solicit from house to house

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertisement containing untruthful, improbable, or impossible statements regarding treatments, cures, or values.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Advertisement in any way in which untruthful, improbable or impossible statements are made regarding treatments, cures or values

disciplinary_grounds.description: Using the term 'eye specialist' in connection with the name of the optometrist.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Inability to demonstrate practical ability to perform any function within the scope of practice that the optometrist utilizes.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Inability to demonstrate, in a manner satisfactory to the secretary or the board of optometry, their practical ability to perform any function set forth in RCW 18.53.010 which they utilize in their practice.

definition_quote.value: The practice of optometry is defined as the examination of the human eye, the examination and ascertaining any defects of the human vision system, and the analysis of the process of vision.
definition_quote.quote: The practice of optometry is defined as the examination of the human eye, the examination and ascertaining any defects of the human vision system, and the analysis of the process of vision.

value: employment of objective or subjective means or method including use of drugs for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes
prescription and fitting of lenses, prisms, therapeutic or refractive contact lenses
prescription and fitting of contact lenses for altering refractive error or treating eye disease
prescription and provision of visual therapy, neuro-optometry rehabilitation, therapeutic aids, subnormal vision therapy, orthoptics
ascertainment of perceptive, neural, muscular, or pathological condition of the visual system
adaptation of prosthetic eyes
ordering diagnostic lab or imaging tests including finger-stick testing and collecting samples for culturing
dispensing of medication samples to initiate treatment

removal of nonpenetrating foreign bodies, debridement of tissue, epilation of misaligned eyelashes, placement of punctal or lacrimal plugs, dilation and irrigation of the lacrimal system, nonlaser light therapy, placement of biologic membranes
methods_authorized.quote: The practice of optometry may include, but not necessarily be limited to, the following: (a) The employment of any objective or subjective means or method, including the use of drugs, for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes

drug_authority.value: Topical and oral drugs for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes, including oral Schedule III-V controlled substances and legend drugs, with board-established lists; Schedule I and II controlled substances prohibited except Schedule II hydrocodone combination products.
drug_authority.quote: The optometry board must establish a list of oral Schedule III through V controlled substances and any oral legend drugs, with the approval of and after consultation with the pharmacy quality assurance commission.

surgery_prohibited.quote: Nothing in this chapter may be construed to authorize optometrists to perform ophthalmic surgery.

surgery_definition.value: Ophthalmic surgery is defined as any invasive procedure in which human tissue is cut, ablated, or otherwise penetrated by incision, injection, laser, ultrasound, or other means, in order to: Treat human eye diseases; alter or correct refractive error; or alter or enhance cosmetic appearance.
surgery_definition.quote: Ophthalmic surgery is defined as any invasive procedure in which human tissue is cut, ablated, or otherwise penetrated by incision, injection, laser, ultrasound, or other means, in order to: Treat human eye diseases; alter or correct refractive error; or alter or enhance cosmetic appearance.

foreign_body_removal_authorized.quote: Removal of nonpenetrating foreign bodies, debridement of tissue, epilation of misaligned eyelashes, placement of punctal or lacrimal plugs

value: light adjustable lens procedures
nonlaser light therapy
diagnostic instruments utilizing laser or ultrasound technology
laser_procedures_authorized.quote: The practice of optometry does not include: (a) Performing retinal laser procedures, laser-assisted in situ keratomileus, photorefractive keratectomy, laser epithelial keratomileusis, or any forms of refractive surgery, other than light adjustable lens procedures

value: Chalazion management, including injection and excision
Injections, including intramuscular injections of epinephrine and subconjunctival and subcutaneous injections of medications
Management of lid lesions, including intralesional injection of medications
Preoperative and postoperative care related to these procedures
Use of topical and injectable anesthetics
Eyelid surgery, excluding cosmetic surgery or surgery requiring general anesthesia
Common complication of the lids, lashes, and lacrimal systems
minor_surgical_procedures_authorized.quote: The practice of optometry may include the following advanced procedures: (i) Common complication of the lids, lashes, and lacrimal systems; (ii) Chalazion management, including injection and excision; (iii) Injections, including intramuscular injections of epinephrine and subconjunctival and subcutaneous injections of medications; (iv) Management of lid lesions, including intralesional injection of medications; (v) Preoperative and postoperative care related to these procedures; (vi) Use of topical and injectable anesthetics; and (vii) Eyelid surgery, excluding any cosmetic surgery or surgery requiring the use of general anesthesia.

anaphylaxis_treatment_authorized.quote: Those persons administering epinephrine by injection for treatment of anaphylactic shock in the practice of optometry must be certified under (b) of this subsection and must have an additional minimum of four hours of didactic and supervised clinical instruction

vision_therapy_authorized.quote: The prescription and provision of visual therapy, neuro-optometry rehabilitation, therapeutic aids, subnormal vision therapy, orthoptics, and other optical devices

immunization_authority.quote: In a public health emergency, the state health officer may authorize licensed optometrists to administer inoculations for systemic health reasons.

value: Schedule I controlled substances prohibited
Schedule II controlled substances prohibited except Schedule II hydrocodone combination products
Oral Schedule III through V controlled substances permitted per board-established list
controlled_substance_schedule_restrictio.quote: Nothing in this chapter may be construed to authorize the use, prescription, dispensing, purchase, possession, or administration of any Schedule I or II controlled substance, except Schedule II hydrocodone combination products.

opioid_prescription_day_limit.quote: An optometrist may not prescribe, dispense, or administer a controlled substance for more than seven days in treating a particular patient for a single trauma, episode, or condition

oral_pharmaceutical_authority.quote: Those persons using or prescribing drugs administered orally for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes in the practice of optometry shall be certified under (b) of this subsection

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: Those persons using topical and oral drugs for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes in the practice of optometry shall have a minimum of 60 hours of didactic and clinical instruction in general and ocular pharmacology as applied to optometry, as established by the optometry board, and certification from an institution of higher learning

tiered_license_types.quote: An optometrist shall not perform any advanced procedures listed in this subsection until he or she receives a license endorsement issued by the optometry board.

supervised_clinical_internship_required.quote: Any course that is offered by an institution of higher education accredited by those agencies recognized by the United States department of education or the council on higher education accreditation and approved by the optometry board to qualify for an endorsement to perform advanced procedures must contain supervised hands-on experience with live patients, or be supplemented by a residency, internship, or other supervised program that offers hands-on experience with live patients

referral_to_physician_required.quote: If treatment exceeding the limitation in (b) of this subsection is indicated, the patient must be referred to a physician licensed under chapter 18.71 RCW.
